newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 5.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Financial and Fiscal Commission yesterday sharply criticised government's macro-economic plan, saying expenditure was being cut too fast and would hit provinces ability to deliver vital services.

- Two consortia have been short-listed for a key Maputo Corridor project - a 30-year 600 million to 800 million rand contract to build and maintain a road between the Gauteng-Mpumalanga border and Maputo.

- Richard Branson's Virgin Atlantic airline, scheduled for take-off in South Africa next month, is set to fly into heavy weather - a price war that has broken out between the international carriers serving South Africa.

- Radio 702 owner Primedia Broadcasting had given itself sweeping powers in a consortium bidding for Gauteng radio station Highveld Stereo - at the expense of its black empowerment partners, the Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA) heard yesterday.
- Almost one-million taxpayers who have not submitted tax returns this year could end up with criminal records.

- South Africa issued a veiled threat to the French government yesterday that business opportunities for its companies would be restricted unless France softened its opposition to South African access to the European market for agricultural produce.

- Virgin Atlantic Airways will announce an alliance with a domestic airline today, believed to be state-owned Sun Air, to complement its service between London and South Africa, which starts next month.

- The gold price would have to reach $500 an ounce to make it worthwhile to mine the bulk of South Africa's remaining gold because of the rising expense of deep mining and increased labour costs, a report by the London-based Economist Intelligence Unit says.
- A 750 million rand designer township will be developed on the virgin slopes of the Twelve Apostles near Camps Bay, but the project could come under fire by environmental and other lobby groups.
- Seven people were killed and eight seriously wounded during a shoot-out between rival taxi organisations in Soshangue and North-West province yesterday.

- Shocked parishioners and members of the public gathered yesterday at the parish of Uniting Church of Southern Africa moderator, Rev Ezekiel Mataboge, who was shot at point-blank range by three assailants.
